title: release.decide is on the shared runtime contract, with its three refusal codes and their closed layer map
description:

THIS IS THE LEAF. `apps/daemon` imports `RuntimeCommandKind` from `@moe/contracts`, so the daemon roster cannot name `release.decide` until this row lands.

- `packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:85` `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS`, sorted; `escalation.decide` sits at :92, `repository.publish` at :109. Insert `release.decide` in SORTED position.
- `packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-contract.test.ts:35` `EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS` (hand list, `:103` `toEqual`) and `:105` `expect(commands.size).toBe(103)`. BOTH move. Do NOT trust the literal 103 in this description - task-40e52fa8 bumps it first; read the printed value and reconcile.
- `packages/control-room-client/src/contract-pins.ts` is a bare RE-EXPORT and `src/contract-digest.test.ts` DERIVES the digest (`:21 expect(deriveContractDigest()).toBe(GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST)`). Neither is hand-edited. `generator/generate.ts:299` writes exactly ONE file: `src/generated/generated-client.ts`.

COLLISION HAZARD, and why dependsOn is set: task-40e52fa8 (WORKING) is landing `preview.decide` through the SAME lines - runtime-vocabulary.ts, EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS, the `commands.size` literal and the generated client. Two rows bumping the same count literal concurrently is a guaranteed conflict. This row waits.

The three refusal codes and their closed code->layer map are HERE, not in the service row, so the service row consumes a contract it cannot disagree with: the factory takes NO layer argument, so a call site is structurally unable to mint a disagreeing (code, layer) pair.
definitionOfDone: `release.decide` is a member of `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` in packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts, in SORTED position, and `runtime-contract.test.ts` agrees in both of its coupled assertions: the `EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS` hand list (`toEqual`) and the `commands.size` literal. The generated client is REGENERATED, never hand-edited: run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate` and quote the OLD and the NEW `GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST` in the completion record. `packages/control-room-client/src/contract-digest.test.ts` derives the digest rather than pinning it, so it must go green WITHOUT being edited - if it needs an edit, the generate step was skipped.

A new `apps/daemon/src/release/release-decide-contracts.ts` declares exactly three refusal codes - RELEASE_REMOTE_MISSING, RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE, RELEASE_PR_FAILED - and ONE frozen code->layer map covering all three. The refusal factory takes the CODE only and reads the layer from that map: it accepts no layer argument, so no call site can mint a disagreeing pair. A test asserts, per code, both the code AND the layer it resolves to.

The layer names reuse EXISTING rostered layer constants or add a properly rostered one - a bare string literal at the throw site is unenumerable by tests/security/boundary-roster.security.ts (see `daemon-command-registry.ts:206` for the existing instance of that hole). If a new `*_LAYER` constant is exported, run `pnpm test:security` and reconcile the roster, its size constant, EXPECTED_DISTRIBUTION, the axis partition and the sibling per-axis pins in ONE commit.

It would also add a 10th file at the hard cap.

IMPORTING the three rostered constants into the production module and using them as the map's values (`layer: PROJECT_REDUCER_LAYER`) — REJECTED for import drag: recovery-completion-evidence.ts pulls @moe/store, @moe/core and the bootstrap ledger, and foundation-attempt-contracts.ts pulls @moe/runner and @moe/scheduler as VALUE imports. Hand-editing generated-client.ts to add the builder — REJECTED, task rail 1, and client-compat.ts:169 catches it at runtime anyway.

Freezing the count 103 and the digest ed325554 from the task description into the plan — REJECTED per task rail 3 and DoD-1: the prerequisite row task-40e52fa8 moves both first. Every step that touches a literal reads the PRINTED expected-vs-received and reconciles to that.
